agent.name: Scene: World
agent.help: Time, place, weather, quests, items and factions — the world around the story.
agent.prompt:
You keep the world state of this roleplay up to date for a side panel. You never write story text.
Read the recent conversation and the current values, then write what changed.

Rules:
- Only record what actually happened in the story. Keep values the story did not change.
- Be concrete and objective: numbers with units, colors, materials, shapes and where on the body. Never use vague or relative words ("tall", "short", "big", "lean", "beautiful", "average") on their own; give the number or the specific detail instead.

sets.name: Standard
sets.help: Time, place, weather, quests, items and factions.

fields.label: Date
fields.help: The story's calendar date. If the story, a character card or the lorebook gives a date, year or era, use it exactly (any past or future year, any calendar). If nothing gives one, choose one that fits the setting and keep it. When the clock passes midnight, move to the next day.

fields.label: Clock
fields.help: 24-hour "HH:MM". Move it forward by how long the events since the current values would really take, never backwards: a few lines of talk or a quick action 1-5 minutes; a normal conversation about 10 minutes; a long talk, a meal, searching a room or a short fight 15-60 minutes; walking a few minutes inside a building, 15-60 minutes across a town, hours to the next village; travelling between towns hours, or days for long journeys; resting or waiting as long as the story says; sleeping through the night: the next morning (usually 06:00-08:00); time skips ("three days later") jump exactly that far. When the story or a character says the time, use it; when unsure, take the smaller jump.

fields.label: Part of the day
fields.help: Must match the clock.

fields.label: Location
fields.help: Short and specific. Keep the old one if nothing changed.

fields.label: Weather
fields.help: Short and specific: temperature, sky, wind. Keep the old one if nothing changed.

fields.label: Quests
fields.help: Add one only when a task or goal is clearly given or taken on. Set the status to completed or failed when the story resolves it.

fields.label: Note
fields.help: one short line on where it stands

fields.label: Items
fields.help: Notable items {{user}} carries, with amount or state when it matters ("waterskin, half full"). Add only items clearly taken, bought or given; remove items lost, used up or given away.

fields.label: Factions
fields.help: The named groups {{user}} has dealt with or heard of. Change the stance only when the story shows it.

fields.label: Stance
fields.help: how they treat {{user}} right now

fields.label: Standing
fields.help: one or two sentences on where they stand and why

agent.name: Scene: Characters
agent.help: Who is here: what they are doing, how they look, and the field set's extras.
agent.prompt:
You track the characters of this roleplay for a side panel: who is in the current scene, and what can be seen and known about each one right now. You never write story text.
Read the recent conversation, the character cards and the current values, then write what changed.

Rules:
- Keep every character. Set "In the scene" to away for anyone who left; never delete anyone.
- Include {{user}} (role: player).
- Add a NEW character only if they have a proper name and actually did or said something in the story (not "the innkeeper" or "a guard"). When in doubt, leave them out.
- Fill every ALWAYS FILLED field from the moment a character is added, so the player can picture them at once: the story first, then the character card or persona. If those do not say, choose values that fit the character, their role and the setting, and keep them.
- Change a value only when the story changes it (new clothes, a wound, a lost weapon). If the story contradicts an earlier choice, the story wins.
- Lorebook entries, character cards and cast sheets are canon for who a character is. When one of them gives a fixed fact (age, height, weight, face, hair, eyes, build, species, powers…), copy it exactly, even if the current values say something else: correct them to match. Things the story changes (clothes, wounds, dirt, mood) follow the story. When the lorebook has rules for new characters (species, height ranges, naming, power limits…), every character you add must follow them. Only invent what none of them and the story give, and keep it inside those rules.
- Be concrete and objective: numbers with units, colors, materials, shapes and where on the body. Never use vague or relative words ("tall", "short", "big", "lean", "beautiful", "average") on their own; give the number or the specific detail instead.

sets.name: Standard
sets.help: Who is here, what they are doing, and how they look.

fields.label: Face
fields.help: Face shape, skin tone and notable features, in concrete terms ("square jaw, light olive skin, freckles across the nose").

fields.label: Hair
fields.help: Color, length and style ("black, shoulder-length, tied back").

fields.label: Eyes
fields.help: Color and shape ("pale grey, narrow").

fields.label: Build
fields.help: Frame and musculature in concrete terms: shoulder width, muscle, body fat, posture. No vague words like "lean" or "fit".

fields.label: Outfit
fields.help: Every visible garment with color and material ("faded green wool cloak over a brown leather jerkin, black trousers, worn boots").

fields.label: Accessories
fields.help: What they carry or wear besides clothes: weapons, jewelry, bags. Empty when there is nothing.

fields.label: Marks
fields.help: Scars, wounds, tattoos, dirt or blood, and where on the body. Empty when there is nothing.

fields.label: In the scene
fields.help: here = in the current scene; away = left or not here. Never delete a character: set away.

fields.label: Role
fields.help: A few words: ally, rival, shopkeeper… {{user}} is the player.

fields.label: Mood
fields.help: A few words about how they feel right now.

fields.label: Where
fields.help: Exactly where in the scene they are ("by the altar", "at the main doors"). For characters away: where they went or were last seen.

fields.label: Posture
fields.help: Standing, sitting, kneeling, lying, walking… Empty for characters away.

fields.label: Distance from {{user}}
fields.help: How far from {{user}}, with a unit ("2 m"). Empty for {{user}} and for characters away.

fields.label: Doing
fields.help: What they are doing right now, a few words ("lighting the candles"). Nobody moves, sits down or stops what they do unless the story shows it.

fields.label: Notes
fields.help: One short line worth remembering.

fields.label: Description
fields.help: One or two sentences on who they are: what they do and where they stand in the story.

fields.label: Traits
fields.help: 3 to 6 short personality traits or drives ("resourceful", "wary", "protective of Mira").

fields.label: Age
fields.help: Age in years as a number ("27"). Long-lived beings: real age and the age they look ("340, looks 30").

fields.label: Height
fields.help: Exact height with unit, metric ("1.83 m"). Giants, children and small creatures get their real number too. Never just "tall" or "short".

fields.label: Weight
fields.help: Exact weight with unit, metric ("82 kg"). Never just "heavy" or "light".

fields.help: The skills they have ready, one per slot: never more rows than Skill slots. Change them only when the story does (learning, swapping, losing one).

agent.name: Scene: Plot
agent.help: Threads, what each character wants, secrets, and your planned beats.
agent.prompt:
You keep the plot notes of this story for the author, in a side panel. You never write story text.
Read the recent conversation, the author's planned beats and the current notes, then write what changed.

Rules:
- Lorebook entries and character cards are canon.
- Only record what the story actually shows.

sets.name: Standard
sets.help: Threads, goals, secrets and your planned beats.

fields.label: Planned beats
fields.help: Your own plan: the beats you want the story to reach, in order. The tracker never changes this list; it marks which ones the story reached.

fields.label: Beats reached
fields.help: Titles of the planned beats the story has now reached, copied exactly. Empty list when none.

fields.label: Threads
fields.help: The open arcs and questions of the story. Keep every thread; change its status only when the story does. Add a thread only when the story clearly opens one.

fields.label: Status
fields.help: brewing = set up, not started yet

fields.label: Note
fields.help: one short line on where it stands

fields.label: Goals
fields.help: One row per named character who matters right now (not {{user}}): what they want and the next thing they will try on their own. Update them when the story changes them.

fields.label: Secrets
fields.help: Facts that some characters know and others don't. Drop a secret once everyone knows it.

fields.label: Known by
fields.help: character names

fields.label: Unaware
fields.help: character names
